title: Edge proxy telemetry handoff and shard coordinator for tenant-aware log ingestion
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Summary:
We need a hardened handoff path from the edge proxy (ingest gateway) to the internal shard coordinator that preserves structured log integrity, deterministic ordering, and correlation IDs while enabling tenant-aware sharding and upstream fanout to Loki/ELK. This ticket implements the edge-side changes and a lightweight shard coordinator service to route batched structured events into the existing ingestion fabric with backpressure and per-tenant ordering tokens. The goal is to reduce noisy cross-tenant fanout, lower tail latency under bursty workloads, and make tracing correlations first-class through the pipeline.

Background:
Current edge proxy simply forwards JSONL events to a monolithic intake which performs tenant demuxing and enrichment. This creates hotspots during tenant bursts and makes deterministic ordering expensive (buffering/rehydration). Observability teams have seen correlated trace gaps when the intake reorders or drops out-of-order batches during partial failures. We also lack an edge-level sampling hook to attach trace/span metadata for low-frequency but high-value debug traces.

Goals:
- Implement an edge-side handoff protocol: signaled batch boundaries, optional sequence-token, and correlation-id headers that are enforced by the shard coordinator.
- Create shard coordinator service that maps tenant -> shard using a stable consistent-hash with tenant affinity and supports in-flight reassignments with graceful draining.
- Ensure per-tenant ordering guarantees via monotonic sequence tokens persisted to a lightweight sequencer (in-memory leader + write-ahead ledger backed by S3/Redis).
- Surface trace/span links at the edge: accept OTEL link headers, normalize trace IDs to canonical 128-bit hex, and append a field "redwood.trace_context" to structured logs.
- Provide integration adapters to forward to Loki and Elasticsearch indices with schema hints and index-key routing.
- Add metrics & dashboards: shard utilization, handoff latency, reorder/drop rates, sequence-token gaps, and top noisy tenants.

Non-goals:
- Do not replace the entire intake fabric. This is an incremental handoff layer and coordinator; long-term intake refactor is separate.
tasks: Design proto: edge->coordinator batch envelope (headers, sequence_token, tenant_id, payload schema_version)
Implement edge proxy encoder changes: batch boundary signals, OTEL header parsing, canonical trace id normalization
Create shard coordinator service: REST gRPC endpoints for claim/release/route and a consistent-hash ring implementation
Sequencer: in-memory leader with WAL to S3 for crash recovery and Redis for fast token lookups
Integration adapter: Loki client with stream labels from tenant and route keys; ES adapter with index aliasing per tenant
Backpressure flow: implement 429/Retry-After at edge and coordinator, circuit-breaker for overloaded shards
Add metrics: handoff_latency_ms, shard_queue_depth, sequence_token_mismatch_count, reorder_events_count
Dashboard: Grafana panels for per-shard P99, tenant hot-shard heatmap, correlation-gap alerting
E2E tests: ordering under failover, sequence token restores, OTEL trace propagation verification
Run canary in eu-west-1 for 48h with 5% traffic, validate no customer impact and stable ordering
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy can emit batched envelopes with sequence_token and redwood.trace_context for sampled traces
Shard coordinator routes >99% of tenant traffic to same shard when no reassignments are occurring
Per-tenant monotonic ordering preserved in 99.99% of test scenarios (simulated failover + reorder injection)
Backpressure path causes edge to return 429 with Retry-After and metrics reflect load rather than silent drops
Loki and ES adapters ingest batched events without schema loss and preserve correlation IDs in the downstream index/streams
Dashboards show correct handoff latency and alerts fire on sequence_token gap > 1 for critical tenants
Canary run (eu-west-1, 5% traffic) reports no client-visible dropped logs and trace linkability improves for sampled traces
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Sequencer leader flip could cause temporary reorder or stalls. Mitigation: WAL to S3 for fast recovery, grace window for sequence acceptance, and bounded retry loops on the coordinator.
Risk: Increased latency during canary due to extra coordinator hop. Mitigation: keep coordinator in same VPC, use UDP-based quick-acks for non-blocking handoff path and allow one-step fast-path for small events.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests; 2) deploy edge proxy changes behind feature flag; 3) deploy shard coordinator in blue/green in eu-west-1; 4) enable 5% canary traffic for 48h; 5) expand to 25% if no issues then 100% in phased regions; 6) deprecate old intake path after 2 weeks of stable operation.
notes: We should coordinate with Security to review trace-context handling (PII risk) and with Privacy to ensure tenant-level indexing doesn't expose cross-tenant visibility. Work with Platform SRE to reserve capacity for coordinator in Dedicated clusters.
comments: 2026-03-02 Avery Kim: Initial design doc posted to Confluence. Added sequencer architecture sketch and trade-offs between Redis-only vs WAL+S3. Asking SRE for capacity estimate.

2026-03-04 Sofia Martinez: Implemented edge header parsing and unit tests for OTEL canonicalization. Opened draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/298. Noted some telemetry field collisions with existing "trace_id" field—proposing "redwood.trace_context" as namespace.
2026-03-06 Raj Patel (SRE): Provided capacity snapshot and suggested 3 replica coordinators per region. Recommended Redis cluster with AOF and read replicas for token lookups.
2026-03-08 Design review (Lena Ortiz): Approved schema but requested an explicit schema_version in the envelope and a compatibility plan for older agents.

2026-03-10 Sofia Martinez: Coordinator service skeleton merged behind feature flag. Integration tests failing intermittently on reorder test; investigating leader election timing and WAL flush ordering. Sequencer WAL flush interval increased from 50ms -> 200ms to reduce false positives in CI.
